function: Learned adaptive spatio-temporal broadband beamforming: a complex CNN predicts the 288 complex weights of the frequency-constrained Frost beamformer from low-snapshot array data. p. 2, 4
system: 16-element ULA, 18 delays per element, one desired signal and one interferer; 300 MHz passband starting at 800 MHz; no RIS. p. 4
method: Complex-valued CNN (BBPCNet): five complex conv layers, complex batch normalization, complex LeakyReLU, FC layer; supervised MSE regression on weights from 4000 snapshots; Adam, PyTorch. p. 2-4
data_channel: Own simulator: ULA with one desired and one interfering broadband source, white Gaussian noise, SNR 0 dB, INR 40 dB; no standard channel or measured data. p. 4
test_conditions: Training: 500 samples per (desired, interference) angle pair at 400 snapshots, labels from 4000 snapshots, 300 epochs; other snapshot numbers trained separately. Test: 10 per pair. p. 4
baselines: Non-learned: FCFB with low and high snapshots. Learned: WBPNet (real CNN, [26]), AlexNet, ResNet-18, Transformer, two real CNNs. p. 3-5
metrics: Beam patterns and output SINR (Table II) versus snapshots and interference angle; 40 Monte Carlo runs. p. 3, 4
complexity: FLOPs formulas per layer (conv: Ho x Co x ke^2 x Ci x Co); FCFB in complex multiplications; no numeric totals or runtime. p. 5
openness: none. No code or data link; PyTorch on an RTX3060 is only mentioned. p. 4
q1_support: p. 4: "One desired broadband signal comes from the direction". Own ULA array model (p. 2, far-field plane wave, Gaussian white noise); no 3GPP, COST 2100 or DeepMIMO channel and no measured data is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 4: "training and test samples are 500 and 10, respectively" for each angle pair; p. 4: "the BBPCNets corresponding to these Nlow are realized respectively under the same training condition". Each snapshot number is a separate training; no model is tested on unseen angles, array size or band.
q3_support: p. 3: "The optimum weights of the FCFB-LS and FCFB-HS are obtained with (9)" (non-learned Frost beamformer); p. 3: "the frequency constraint wideband beamforming prediction network (WBPNet)" (earlier learned CNN [26]), plus AlexNet, ResNet-18, Transformer; output SINR compared in Table II (p. 4).
q4_support: p. 5: "In CCONV layers, the computational complexity equals to" Ho x Co x ke^2 x Ci x Co, with an FC-layer formula and FLOPs counted. No numeric total, parameter count or runtime is given, and the "far lower" claim is qualitative.
q5_support: p. 4: "The training of BBPCNet is conducted in Pytorch with RTX3060". Data are simulated (p. 4); no code or data link, public dataset or measured data appears in the paper.
notes: Include, area 3: the learned network outputs beamforming weights, and the abstract (p. 1) frames the work for mmWave massive MIMO. The simulation (p. 4) is a generic ULA scenario at 800 MHz and above with one desired signal and one interferer, the metric is output SINR, and no data symbols or communication link are simulated; p. 4 also says "DOA of jamming". The reviewer should confirm that the function belongs to area 3 and not outside the scope. q3: WBPNet [26] shares authors with this paper only by the reference list (p. 5), not by an explicit statement. q4 is marked 1 for the FLOPs formulas only; the reviewer should confirm.
